newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa may test highs again.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa may test highs again.

text.p: MAY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Cocoa may be ready to retest highs on May after its tumble early last week, technical analysts said.
It looked likely to hold above last week's low of 962 stg a tonne, they said.
Traders called the market unchanged to 2 stg lower.

"On balance the market looks as though it should definitely hold above 962 stg, and there's a chance the 1,050 high will be tested," Adrian Haylor, technical analyst at Sucden, said. Last week's fall could be seen as a correction+ "if you want to be bullish," he said.
But he stressed that cocoa might test the highs. "On balance the market looks reasonably firm, but I'm not that convinced," he said.
On Friday, New York ended firmer, but prices drifted off the highs after buying subsided and scattered speculative profit-taking and trade sales emerged in the afternoon, dealers said.
Traders were also encouraged by both the ability of the London and U.S. markets to hold steady after sharp sell-offs.

After New York's close Friday, the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report for the two weeks ended April 8 showed non-commercial long positions decreased by 2,130 lots, to 16,537, while non-commercial short positions increased by 65 lots, to 3,371 lots.
Traders said the report, which showed speculators (non-commercials and nonreportables) were net long 22,266 lots, was within expectations.
